components.css: .ds-nav { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: clamp(28px, 4.2vw, 66px); font-family: var(--font-body); font-size: 18px; } .ds-nav a { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; min-height: 44px; min-width: 44px; justify-content: center; color: var(--ink); text-decoration: none; text-underline-offset: 6px; } .ds-nav a:hover, .ds-nav a:focus-visible, .ds-nav a[aria-current] { color: var(--green); text-decoration: underline; } .ds-nav .ds-nav-hello { color: var(--green); text-decoration: underline; text-decoration-thickness: 1px; } .ds-nav a:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--green); outline-offset: 6px; border-radius: 2px; } @media (max-width: 700px) { .ds-nav { width: 100%; justify-content: space-between; gap: 12px; font-size: 16px; } } .ds-nav .ds-nav-hello { padding: 10px 20px; min-height: 48px; border-radius: 4px; background: var(--sage); color: var(--paper); font-weight: 500; line-height: 1.4; text-decoration: underline; text-underline-offset: 4px; } .ds-nav .ds-nav-hello:hover, .ds-nav .ds-nav-hello:active { color: var(--paper); background: var(--sage-hover); } @media (max-width: 700px) { .ds-nav .ds-nav-hello { min-height: 44px; padding: 8px 12px; } }

components.css: .ds-project { position: relative; display: grid; grid-template-columns: 47% 1fr; gap: 20px; min-height: 192px; align-items: start; padding: 0 32px; border-right: 1px solid var(--rule); font-family: var(--font-body); } .ds-project-media { display: grid; place-items: center; width: 100%; height: 165px; background: var(--soft); } .ds-project-plate { display: block; width: 72%; height: 58%; border: 1px solid var(--rule); background: var(--paper); } .ds-project-copy { min-width: 0; padding-top: 5px; } .ds-project h2 { margin: 0; color: var(--ink); font-size: 30px; line-height: 1.1; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: -.025em; } .ds-project h2 a { color: inherit; text-decoration: none; } .ds-project h2 a:hover, .ds-project h2 a:focus-visible { color: var(--green); } .ds-project-arrow { width: 22px; vertical-align: middle; color: var(--green); transition: transform 180ms ease; } .ds-project h2 a:hover .ds-project-arrow, .ds-project h2 a:focus-visible .ds-project-arrow { transform: translateX(4px); } .ds-project p { margin: 14px 0 0; color: var(--ink); font-size: 17px; line-height: 26px; } .ds-project-note { display: inline-block; margin-top: 16px; color: var(--green); font-family: var(--font-note); font-size: 25px; line-height: 1.2; } @media (max-width: 700px) { .ds-project { grid-template-columns: 128px minmax(0, 1fr); gap: 20px; min-height: 194px; padding: 24px 0; border-right: 0; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--rule); } .ds-project-media { width: 128px; height: 128px; } .ds-project h2 { font-size: 24px; } .ds-project p { margin-top: 10px; font-size: 16px; line-height: 23px; } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-project-arrow { transition: none; } }

components.name: Reading Page
components.description: Centered project and note copy with a spacious, rule-led reading rhythm.
components.html:
Back to creations

Project Drift

A word-association game I’m testing.

Project Drift is a word-association game I’m currently testing. The loop is simple: you get two word prompts, respond with the first association that comes to mind, then receive a new word to continue.

I’m curious about what happens when a game gives you a small prompt and lets your mind take it somewhere unexpected.
components.css: .ds-reading { width: min(100%, 720px); margin-inline: auto; font-family: var(--font-body); color: var(--ink); } .ds-reading-back { display: inline-flex; min-height: 44px; align-items: center; gap: 8px; color: var(--green); text-decoration: underline; text-underline-offset: 9px; } .ds-reading-back-arrow { flex: none; transform: rotate(180deg); } .ds-reading h1 { margin: 30px 0 20px; font-size: clamp(36px, 4vw, 56px); line-height: 1.15; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: -.025em; } .ds-reading-description { max-width: 32ch; color: var(--muted); font-size: 24px; line-height: 1.45; } .ds-reading-prose { margin-top: 40px; max-width: 68ch; font-size: 20px; line-height: 1.75; } .ds-reading-prose p { margin-block: 1.25em; } .ds-reading-prose p:first-child { margin-top: 0; } .ds-reading-prose p:last-child { margin-bottom: 0; } .ds-reading a:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--green); outline-offset: 6px; border-radius: 2px; } @media (max-width: 700px) { .ds-reading-description { font-size: 21px; } .ds-reading-prose { font-size: 18px; } }

narrative.overview:
NewLad Creations presents Karim through the things he makes: a bright, daytime studio with room for experiments, unfinished work, and short notes. The implemented homepage opens with a candid original color portrait, a clear introduction, and a direct path into three creations. White space, black type, and one plant-green thread keep the page personal and easy to enter.

Material character comes from local concept-art plates, a cedar-and-stone visual temperature in the imagery, fine gray rules, and one handwritten Caveat accent. Interior creation and note pages keep the same light canvas and move into a centered reading column. Motion is brief and optional: one underline draws in and arrows shift slightly, with a reduced-motion fallback.
keyCharacteristics: Bright white studio canvas with black text and plant-green links.
Candid original portrait in a circle and optimized local image plates.
Kedebideri for display and body copy, with Caveat for short process marks.
Open desktop grids that become linear, touch-friendly sections on mobile.
Fine gray rules and whitespace provide structure; surfaces stay flat.

rules.name: The Green Thread Rule
rules.body: Plant green is reserved for navigation state, linked action, underlines, and handwritten annotations; the deeper green is a hover state.

rules.name: The Light Studio Rule
rules.body: Paper is the default canvas. Soft neutrals support feedback and quiet surfaces without turning the page into a card stack.

rules.name: The Handmade Accent Rule
rules.body: Use Caveat only for a short annotation or process cue; keep explanations, navigation, and project titles in Kedebideri.

rules.name: The Flat-by-Default Rule
rules.body: Keep UI surfaces flat at rest; use whitespace, rules, imagery, and restrained state changes to create depth.

dos: Do keep the page on paper white with ink-black text and a plant-green interaction thread.
Do preserve the original color portrait as a circular image and keep local image plates optimized.
Do label concept artwork and game concept imagery so it reads as illustrative context rather than working hardware or a product screenshot.
Do use one-pixel cedar-gray rules, open spacing, and the responsive grid-to-linear rhythm to organize content.
Do keep the underline entrance and arrow movement optional, with the reduced-motion fallback intact.
Do retain the cube mark in the footer as a meaningful NewLad Creations identity element.
donts: Don't add pill controls, rounded cards, box shadows, or decorative gradients to this flat studio system.
Don't replace Kedebideri body and display text with a system display face; use Caveat only for short handwritten annotations.
Don't treat concept artwork as documentary photography or imply a project is more finished than the copy says.
Don't add newly public health or therapy details to copy, imagery, metadata, or project stories.
Don't make motion necessary to understand a link or section; all content and navigation must remain available with reduced motion.
